name: Brainstorming
description: Generate and compare multiple solution options before selecting or specifying one.
purpose: Expand the option space without prematurely committing to the first plausible design.
problem_solved: Teams anchor on an inherited solution and miss simpler, safer or better-evidenced alternatives.
when_to_use: The problem is understood but the solution is unsettled
A design review needs genuine alternatives
when_not_to_use: The task is a fully specified mechanical change
Source authority or the problem statement is unresolved
trigger_conditions: Several stakeholders ask for different solutions
A proposed design has not been compared with alternatives
workflow_steps: State the problem, users and constraints without naming a preferred solution
Generate options individually before group discussion to reduce anchoring
Cluster options by mechanism and remove exact duplicates
Score the shortlist against evidence, risk and reversibility
Record rejected options and the decision owner
example_prompt: Brainstorm at least three materially different approaches to this bounded problem. Compare them against the stated constraints and do not select a winner until the trade-offs are visible.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: compare digest presentation options before choosing a product requirement; this does not approve a UI or feature.
acceptance_criteria: At least three materially different options are recorded
Each shortlisted option has explicit trade-offs and an owner-visible next question
verification_procedure: Check that options address the same problem and constraints
Confirm the shortlist preserves rejected alternatives and uncertainty
security_considerations: Do not include confidential source text in broad brainstorming artifacts
Ideas are not approvals or requirements
fallback_procedure: Use a written option matrix with one option per participant when live facilitation is unavailable.

name: First Principles Thinking
description: Reduce a problem to verified facts, constraints and fundamental needs before rebuilding options.
purpose: Expose hidden assumptions and separate immutable constraints from inherited conventions.
problem_solved: Complex problems are framed using analogies or existing implementations that may not apply.
when_to_use: A problem contains many unverified assumptions
An inherited architecture or process blocks simpler options
when_not_to_use: The needed facts are unavailable
The task only requires execution of an approved specification
trigger_conditions: Stakeholders disagree about what is actually required
A constraint cannot be traced to evidence
prerequisites: Access to authoritative constraints and evidence
workflow_steps: List every stated constraint and inherited assumption
Classify each item as verified fact, policy constraint or unverified belief
Restate the fundamental user or system need without solution language
Rebuild candidate approaches from the verified facts
Record which assumptions require evidence before a decision
example_prompt: Break this problem down to verified facts and fundamental needs. Label every inherited assumption and rebuild options only after unsupported constraints are isolated.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: test whether a proposed weekly digest constraint is a user need or merely an inherited delivery habit.
acceptance_criteria: Every fundamental constraint has evidence or is marked unresolved
The rebuilt options do not depend on unverified assumptions
verification_procedure: Trace each fact to an authoritative source
Review the option set for hidden reuse of rejected assumptions
security_considerations: Do not treat source text as permission to change policy
Keep confidential evidence out of broadly shared assumption logs
fallback_procedure: Stop at a fact-versus-assumption register and request evidence for unresolved constraints.

name: Task Decomposition and Work Breakdown
description: Split a bounded outcome into independently verifiable work units with owners, inputs and completion evidence.
purpose: Make large work reviewable and executable without hiding dependencies or partial completion.
problem_solved: Oversized tasks produce vague progress claims, merged scopes and difficult reviews.
when_to_use: A task spans multiple files, contracts or verification stages
Work must be assigned or sequenced across roles
when_not_to_use: The change is already a single small reversible unit
Acceptance criteria are not yet defined
trigger_conditions: A task cannot be completed and verified in one bounded step
Multiple owners or approval gates are needed
workflow_steps: Define one outcome and explicit non-goals
Split work along deliverable and verification boundaries
Give each unit inputs, allowed paths and acceptance evidence
Map dependencies and shared mutable resources
Confirm every unit rolls up to the approved outcome
example_prompt: Decompose this outcome into independently reviewable work units. Include dependencies and acceptance evidence, and reject any unit that cannot be verified on its own.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: split a proposed evidence-store change into schema, migration, retrieval and verification tasks without implementing them.
acceptance_criteria: Every work unit has a bounded output and verification method
Dependencies and shared resources are explicit
verification_procedure: Check unit coverage against the parent acceptance criteria
Inspect the dependency map for cycles and hidden shared writes
security_considerations: Decomposition must not split approvals into bypassable steps
Sensitive work units need explicit access boundaries
fallback_procedure: Use a checklist of deliverables and checks, then sequence them manually until formal task contracts exist.

name: Vertical Slice Development
description: Deliver one thin end-to-end path through all required layers before broadening feature coverage.
purpose: Validate architecture, contracts and user value with the smallest complete system path.
problem_solved: Layer-by-layer work accumulates unintegrated components and delays discovery of contract failures.
when_to_use: A new product path or integration must be proven end to end
Architecture assumptions need a working acceptance path
when_not_to_use: The work is an isolated internal refactor
Required infrastructure or authorization is unavailable
trigger_conditions: A feature crosses UI, service, data and verification boundaries
A proof of value needs observable behavior rather than component completion
workflow_steps: Choose one observable user outcome and its acceptance scenario
Identify the minimum contract at every layer
Implement only the thin path with synthetic or approved data
Run the end-to-end scenario including failure handling
Record integration findings and defer broader cases to follow-up slices
example_prompt: Define and implement one thin vertical slice for this approved outcome. Include every required layer and a runnable acceptance scenario, but exclude unrelated breadth.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: prove one evidence item flowing from an approved fixture to a cited draft without enabling live collection or publication.
acceptance_criteria: The selected scenario crosses all declared layers
End-to-end success and one failure path have evidence
verification_procedure: Run the golden-path fixture through the complete slice
Inspect logs, contracts and persisted state for missing handoffs
security_considerations: Use synthetic data and least-privilege credentials
A thin slice must not bypass source, publication or approval controls
fallback_procedure: Use contract fakes at unavailable boundaries and mark the slice as not end-to-end verified.

name: Risk-Based Planning
description: Prioritize discovery, controls and sequencing by likelihood, impact and uncertainty rather than task order alone.
purpose: Reduce high-impact uncertainty early and make residual risk visible in the plan.
problem_solved: Plans optimize for easy tasks while postponing the assumptions most likely to invalidate delivery.
when_to_use: Work has material technical, security, data or delivery uncertainty
Several risks compete for limited validation effort
when_not_to_use: The change is low risk and fully specified
Risk ratings would be invented without evidence
trigger_conditions: A plan contains unvalidated dependencies or high-impact failure modes
A migration, integration or external boundary is proposed
workflow_steps: Enumerate risks with cause, event and consequence
Rate likelihood and impact using available evidence
Place high-uncertainty or high-impact validation before dependent implementation
Assign a control, owner and residual-risk decision for each material risk
Reassess the plan when evidence changes a rating
example_prompt: Create a risk-ranked plan for this change. Show which uncertainties must be tested first, who owns each control and what residual risk requires approval.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: prioritize source-authorization and citation-integrity risks before planning a live connector; no live collection is authorized.
acceptance_criteria: Every material risk has an owner and response
High-impact uncertainties precede dependent implementation
verification_procedure: Compare the plan with the risk register and dependency graph
Confirm residual-risk decisions cite evidence and an approver
security_considerations: Do not downgrade security or privacy risks to meet schedule
Risk acceptance requires an authorized human decision
fallback_procedure: Sequence the highest-impact validation first and keep unrated risks explicitly unresolved.

name: Hybrid Retrieval and Search
description: Combine exact keyword or symbol search with semantic retrieval, then fuse and verify candidates.
purpose: Recover both precise terms and conceptually related evidence while keeping provenance visible.
problem_solved: Keyword-only search misses paraphrases while semantic-only search misses exact identifiers and rare terms.
when_to_use: Queries mix identifiers, natural language and domain concepts
A corpus is large enough that one retrieval mode leaves recall gaps
when_not_to_use: Exact path or symbol search already resolves the task
No authorized index or corpus exists
trigger_conditions: Initial exact search returns incomplete evidence
Semantic candidates cannot be tied to authoritative spans
workflow_steps: Run exact search for identifiers, paths and quoted terms
Run semantic retrieval within the same authorization filters
Fuse candidates with a documented rank or score rule
Inspect original spans and remove inaccessible or irrelevant evidence
Record query, index version, filters and final selection
example_prompt: Retrieve evidence for this query using exact and semantic search. Fuse the candidates transparently, preserve source spans and do not infer facts from scores alone.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: combine exact marketplace-policy terms with semantic evidence search while excluding unapproved sources.
acceptance_criteria: Both retrieval modes and their filters are recorded
Every selected candidate has an inspectable source span
verification_procedure: Repeat the query against a fixed corpus snapshot
Check exact-term recall, semantic relevance and access filtering
security_considerations: Apply authorization filters before retrieval and fusion
Do not send private corpus text to an unapproved embedding provider
fallback_procedure: Use exact search plus manual concept expansion and document the reduced recall limitation.

name: Prompt Caching
description: Place stable, reusable prompt content in a provider-supported cacheable prefix and keep volatile content after it.
purpose: Reduce repeated processing of unchanged instructions or evidence when the selected provider supports caching.
problem_solved: Stable context is reprocessed on every request or is mixed with changing data in ways that prevent reuse.
when_to_use: Repeated requests share a large stable prefix
Provider cache semantics and data-retention policy are known
when_not_to_use: The provider does not support caching
The prefix changes every request or contains sensitive data disallowed by policy
trigger_conditions: Profiling shows repeated stable prompt content
A provider documents cacheable prefixes and invalidation behavior
workflow_steps: Identify content that is stable across the intended request family
Verify provider cache boundaries, retention and minimum-size rules
Place stable content before volatile task data
Version the prefix and invalidate it when authority or instructions change
Compare behavior and provider-reported usage without inventing metrics
example_prompt: Propose a cacheable prompt layout for these repeated requests. Separate stable policy and evidence from volatile input, and mark cache hits or savings unknown unless the provider reports them.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: reuse an approved citation-policy prefix across digest drafts only after provider retention and source confidentiality are reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: Stable and volatile regions are explicit and versioned
No cache or cost benefit is claimed without provider evidence
verification_procedure: Inspect prompt ordering and prefix hashes
Run repeated approved requests and compare outputs plus reported usage metadata
security_considerations: Cached content may persist beyond a session
Do not cache secrets, private source text or tenant-mixed evidence
fallback_procedure: Use the normal scoped context pack and record caching as unavailable rather than estimating savings.

name: Incremental Indexing
description: Update a search or retrieval index only for changed, added and deleted artifacts while preserving index version evidence.
purpose: Keep retrieval current without rebuilding an unchanged corpus or silently losing deletions.
problem_solved: Full reindexing wastes work while stale indexes return obsolete code, documents or evidence.
when_to_use: A repository or corpus changes between retrieval runs
Index update cost or freshness matters
when_not_to_use: The index format or parser changed incompatibly
No reliable change set can be established
trigger_conditions: A commit, file hash set or source snapshot differs from the indexed baseline
Search results reference deleted or superseded content
workflow_steps: Compare current hashes with the indexed manifest
Classify additions, modifications and deletions
Reparse only changed compatible artifacts
Remove deleted entries and resolve renamed paths
Verify index version, counts and representative queries
example_prompt: Update this index from the observed change set only. Preserve deletion handling and report the index version and verification queries; rebuild fully only if parser compatibility fails.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: refresh an authorized evidence index after source snapshots change without crawling new domains.
acceptance_criteria: Changed, added and deleted artifacts are accounted for
Representative queries return current authorized content
verification_procedure: Compare index manifests before and after the update
Query one added, modified and deleted fixture and inspect results
security_considerations: Deletion must remove sensitive content from all searchable index layers
Do not index ignored originals or unauthorized sources
fallback_procedure: Perform a full rebuild on a disposable index when the delta cannot be proven complete.

name: Tool Output Filtering
description: Reduce raw tool output to task-relevant, redacted evidence while retaining exit status, counts and failure context.
purpose: Prevent logs from flooding context or hiding the signal needed for a decision.
problem_solved: Verbose terminal or tool responses consume context, leak sensitive data and obscure failures.
when_to_use: A tool can emit large logs, search results or traces
Only selected evidence is needed for the next step
when_not_to_use: A complete audit requires bounded full output
Filtering would remove the only failure evidence
trigger_conditions: Raw output exceeds the declared context or output budget
A tool result contains repetitive or irrelevant records
workflow_steps: Capture exit status and output size before filtering
Select lines or records tied to the task and failure state
Redact secrets and unnecessary personal data
Retain first and last relevant errors plus omission counts
Provide a path to the bounded original when further inspection is authorized
example_prompt: Filter this tool output for evidence relevant to the declared check. Preserve exit status and failure context, report omissions and redactions, and do not silently truncate the only error.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: reduce a future validator log to failing record IDs and summaries without exposing confidential source content.
acceptance_criteria: Exit status and material errors survive filtering
Omissions and redactions are quantified and reviewable
verification_procedure: Compare filtered output with the bounded original
Test success, failure, secret-bearing and over-limit fixtures
security_considerations: Filtering is not a substitute for access control
Retained originals need bounded storage and restricted access
fallback_procedure: Return the exit code and a bounded head-and-tail excerpt with an explicit incomplete-output warning.

name: Session Summarization
description: Create a compact, evidence-linked summary of decisions, changes, checks, blockers and next actions for continuation.
purpose: Preserve durable session state without carrying the entire conversation forward.
problem_solved: Long sessions lose critical constraints or resume from an inaccurate narrative summary.
when_to_use: Context compaction approaches
A session ends or transfers to another worker
when_not_to_use: The session contains no durable decision or action
A full audit trail is required instead of a summary
trigger_conditions: The conversation exceeds the usable context budget
A handoff or resume point is reached
workflow_steps: Extract observed decisions, changes and command results
Separate completed, attempted and unverified work
Link each durable claim to a file, command or source pointer
Record blockers, approvals and the exact next action
Check the summary against current repository state
example_prompt: Summarize this session for safe continuation. Preserve evidence pointers, distinguish executed from planned work and list unresolved approvals and the next action.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: hand off a proposed digest-contract review without implying that a product workflow was executed.
acceptance_criteria: No summary claim lacks an evidence pointer
Pending and unverified work is clearly separated
verification_procedure: Compare the summary with the execution trace and current Git state
Have a second reader identify the next action without replaying the session
security_considerations: Exclude secrets and unnecessary source text
Summaries must not upgrade proposals into approved requirements
fallback_procedure: Use a manual handoff containing exact Git state, commands, outcomes, blockers and next action.

name: Hierarchical Memory
description: Organize durable knowledge into scoped tiers with explicit promotion, retrieval, expiry and conflict rules.
purpose: Reuse approved knowledge across sessions without mixing global policy, project facts and transient observations.
problem_solved: Flat memory stores stale or conflicting facts and leak information across task or tenant boundaries.
when_to_use: Multiple sessions need reusable project or user preferences
Knowledge has different authority, lifetime or access scopes
when_not_to_use: Only one short task requires context
No ownership, expiry or access policy exists
trigger_conditions: The same approved fact is repeatedly re-established
Memory retrieval returns conflicting or cross-scope information
workflow_steps: Classify each fact as global policy, project knowledge, task state or transient observation
Attach source, owner, scope and expiry metadata
Promote only verified reusable facts to higher tiers
Retrieve the narrowest authorized tier needed for the task
Expire or quarantine stale and conflicting records
example_prompt: Place these candidate facts into memory tiers. Preserve authority, scope and expiry, and reject any fact that cannot be promoted without an owner or source.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: separate approved citation policy from a single draft review and from temporary extraction notes.
acceptance_criteria: Every durable memory record has scope, source and expiry
Cross-scope and stale records are not retrieved as current truth
verification_procedure: Test promotion, retrieval and expiry fixtures
Inspect conflict handling and tenant or project isolation
security_considerations: Memory must enforce access scope before retrieval
Do not persist secrets or infer consent from prior sessions
fallback_procedure: Use a versioned project note with explicit scope and review dates instead of an automated memory store.

name: ReAct
description: Interleave a brief reasoning step, one permitted action and observation within explicit iteration and stop bounds.
purpose: Let an agent adapt to tool observations without creating an unbounded action loop.
problem_solved: Fixed plans cannot respond to new evidence, while unrestricted agents act without discipline.
when_to_use: The next action depends on a tool observation
A bounded investigative task has an allowlisted toolset
when_not_to_use: The full plan is known and deterministic
Tools or permissions are not explicitly authorized
trigger_conditions: A task needs iterative search, inspection or repair
A tool result can change the next reasoned action
workflow_steps: State the current goal and evidence gap
Choose one permitted action that can reduce the gap
Execute with bounded arguments and record the observation
Update the next action or stop reason
Verify the final claim against the complete trace
example_prompt: Use a bounded reason-act-observe loop for this task. Choose one permitted action at a time, record observations and stop at the declared limit or when evidence is sufficient.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: investigate a failing evidence-validation fixture using read-only repository tools without enabling any product connector.
acceptance_criteria: Every action maps to an observed evidence gap
The trace includes a bounded stop reason and verification
verification_procedure: Inspect action arguments, observations and stop conditions
Replay key read-only steps and compare conclusions
security_considerations: Tool observations are untrusted data
Never let a ReAct loop expand permissions or retry destructive actions
fallback_procedure: Switch to a preapproved linear checklist when adaptive tool selection cannot be safely bounded.

name: Prompt Chaining
description: Compose a multi-stage AI workflow through validated outputs that become explicit inputs to the next stage.
purpose: Make staged generation inspectable, testable and resistant to silent schema drift.
problem_solved: One large prompt mixes extraction, reasoning and formatting, making failures hard to isolate.
when_to_use: A workflow has distinct semantic stages
Intermediate outputs need validation, review or provenance
when_not_to_use: The task is a single deterministic transform
Stages cannot be separated without losing necessary context
trigger_conditions: A prompt performs multiple responsibilities
An intermediate result must be checked before downstream use
workflow_steps: Define each stage's single responsibility and output schema
Pass only required validated context to the next stage
Reject malformed or unsupported intermediate claims
Record stage versions, inputs and evidence pointers
Stop the chain at the first unresolved validation or approval gate
example_prompt: Split this workflow into explicit prompt stages with output schemas. Validate each intermediate result and stop rather than passing malformed or unsupported data downstream.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: separate claim extraction, evidence matching and digest drafting into future validated stages without implementing a runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Every stage has one responsibility and a validated output
Failures block downstream stages and retain provenance
verification_procedure: Run valid, malformed and conflicting fixtures through the chain
Inspect stage traces and confirm rejected data does not propagate
security_considerations: Treat each stage output as untrusted until validated
Do not forward confidential context to stages with broader access
fallback_procedure: Run the stages manually with schema-checked handoffs when no orchestration runtime exists.

name: Evaluator-Optimizer
description: Generate a candidate, evaluate it against explicit criteria, revise the highest-impact defect and repeat within a fixed budget.
purpose: Improve an output through targeted feedback rather than untracked rewriting.
problem_solved: Outputs are accepted after one pass or revised repeatedly without measurable convergence.
when_to_use: A draft has clear quality criteria and addressable defects
Evaluation can produce actionable, evidence-linked feedback
when_not_to_use: No reliable rubric exists
The task requires factual verification rather than stylistic optimization
trigger_conditions: A candidate fails one or more stated criteria
A bounded number of revision rounds is authorized
workflow_steps: Freeze the candidate version and rubric
Evaluate each criterion with cited defects
Select the smallest revision that addresses the highest-impact defect
Re-evaluate the revised version against the same rubric
Stop on acceptance, no improvement or the round limit
example_prompt: Evaluate this candidate against the fixed rubric, revise only the highest-impact defect and repeat within the declared round limit. Preserve each version and evaluation result.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: improve a draft's structure and citation completeness without allowing the optimizer to invent missing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Each revision maps to a cited evaluation finding
The loop stops on acceptance, no improvement or the fixed limit
verification_procedure: Compare version history with the rubric results
Confirm unsupported claims were rejected rather than optimized away
security_considerations: Optimization must not remove safety, approval or provenance constraints
Evaluator feedback is not factual proof
fallback_procedure: Return the best version with unresolved criteria and request human editing instead of continuing unbounded optimization.

name: Reflection
description: Review an executed trace against intent and evidence to identify failure patterns and a bounded corrective action.
purpose: Turn completed work into explicit learning without rewriting history or claiming unsupported success.
problem_solved: Agents repeat mistakes because post-run review is absent, vague or detached from evidence.
when_to_use: A task, experiment or verification run has completed
A failure or near miss needs a durable lesson
when_not_to_use: No execution trace exists
Reflection would delay an urgent stop or escalation
trigger_conditions: A run ends with failure, surprise or a checkpoint
A repeated failure pattern is suspected
workflow_steps: Restate the intended outcome and actual observed outcome
Identify the first divergent decision or missing check
Classify the failure as evidence, planning, tool, permission or scope related
Propose one bounded corrective action with an owner
Record the lesson separately from any unverified root-cause claim
example_prompt: Reflect on this completed trace against the original intent. Cite the first divergence, distinguish observed facts from hypotheses and propose one bounded corrective action.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: review why a future digest validation draft omitted an effective-date check without claiming the product pipeline exists.
acceptance_criteria: Reflection cites exact trace evidence
Corrective actions are bounded and do not rewrite the execution record
verification_procedure: Compare the reflection with raw outcomes and acceptance criteria
Check that hypotheses are labeled and assigned validation steps
security_considerations: Do not copy secrets into reflection notes
Self-critique does not replace independent review for high-risk work
fallback_procedure: Write a short observed-facts and next-action note when a full reflection cannot be completed.

name: Cost-aware Model Routing and Cascading
description: Route tasks to the least-cost approved model tier that meets evidence-based quality and policy requirements, escalating only on defined signals.
purpose: Control model spend and latency without silently lowering quality or bypassing data policy.
problem_solved: Every request uses an expensive model or weak models fail silently on tasks that need stronger reasoning.
when_to_use: Multiple approved model tiers exist
Fixed evaluations can justify routing thresholds
when_not_to_use: No approved alternatives or evaluation baseline exists
Data policy permits only one provider or model
trigger_conditions: Task classes have different complexity or risk
A cheaper tier can be evaluated against a stable rubric
workflow_steps: Classify task complexity, risk and data-handling needs
Filter to policy-approved models before considering cost
Select the cheapest tier with sufficient evaluation evidence
Escalate only on explicit validation, confidence or rubric signals
Record the route, versions, reported usage and final quality result
example_prompt: Route this task through approved model tiers using evidence-based thresholds. Escalate only on the declared signals and do not claim savings or quality without recorded results.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: evaluate cheaper routing for routine draft formatting while keeping claim verification on an approved stronger tier; no provider call is authorized here.
acceptance_criteria: Policy filtering precedes cost selection
Every escalation has a recorded signal and outcome
verification_procedure: Run the fixed task set through each approved route
Compare quality, failures and provider-reported usage against the baseline
security_considerations: Never route restricted data to a cheaper but disallowed provider
Model confidence alone is not an escalation or acceptance guarantee
fallback_procedure: Use the single approved baseline model and mark routing benefits unknown until comparative evidence exists.

name: Ensemble Verification
description: Use multiple independent verification methods or perspectives and reconcile disagreements with evidence.
purpose: Reduce single-reviewer blind spots without treating agreement as proof.
problem_solved: One reviewer or checker misses defects that a different method or context would expose.
when_to_use: High-impact claims need independent checks
Different verifiers can test distinct properties or failure modes
when_not_to_use: Verifiers share the same hidden context or tool failure
A deterministic check fully covers the acceptance criterion
trigger_conditions: A claim is consequential or disputed
A single verification method has known blind spots
workflow_steps: Assign distinct checks or contexts to each verifier
Collect findings without exposing other verdicts
Compare agreements and disagreements by property
Resolve conflicts with deterministic evidence or human review
Report residual uncertainty instead of manufacturing consensus
example_prompt: Verify this artifact with independent checks for correctness, security and acceptance. Reconcile disagreements using evidence and do not convert majority agreement into proof.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: independently check a future digest's citations, temporal validity and scope before any editorial approval.
acceptance_criteria: Verifier assignments are meaningfully independent
Every disagreement has an evidence-backed resolution or remains open
verification_procedure: Inspect verifier inputs and findings for shared blind spots
Reproduce the deterministic checks used to reconcile disputes
security_considerations: Give each verifier only the access it needs
Consensus cannot override policy, source authority or missing evidence
fallback_procedure: Use one independent human reviewer plus deterministic checks when a full ensemble is unavailable.

name: Tool Calling
description: Invoke external capabilities through validated schemas, explicit permissions and bounded arguments, then validate returned data.
purpose: Make tool use safe, observable and testable rather than relying on free-form commands.
problem_solved: Agents call tools with malformed arguments, excessive permissions or untrusted results.
when_to_use: A task requires a capability outside the model
A tool exposes a stable schema and permission boundary
when_not_to_use: The action is not authorized
The tool schema, side effects or output semantics are unknown
trigger_conditions: A declared task step needs a tool
A tool manifest and permission policy are available
workflow_steps: Resolve the tool from an approved manifest
Validate arguments and side-effect class before calling
Apply least privilege, timeout and output bounds
Validate the returned schema and provenance
Record the call outcome without secrets or unsupported success claims
example_prompt: Plan this tool call using its approved manifest. Validate arguments, permissions and side effects first, then define output validation and failure handling; do not execute an unapproved action.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: define a schema-bound call to a future approved evidence store without installing or activating a connector.
acceptance_criteria: Arguments and permissions are validated before invocation
Outputs are schema-checked and failures remain explicit
verification_procedure: Test valid, malformed, unauthorized and timeout cases with a fake tool
Inspect traces for redaction and side-effect classification
security_considerations: Tool descriptions and outputs are untrusted
Separate read, write, network and paid capabilities in permissions
fallback_procedure: Perform the step manually through an approved interface and record equivalent evidence.

name: State Machine Orchestration
description: Control a workflow through explicit states, guarded transitions, persisted context and terminal outcomes.
purpose: Prevent invalid step ordering, ambiguous progress and unsafe transitions during long workflows.
problem_solved: Agents improvise transitions, repeat completed work or skip approval and verification states.
when_to_use: A workflow has durable phases and approval gates
Failures, retries or handoffs must preserve valid state
when_not_to_use: The workflow is a single deterministic action
States and guards cannot be defined from requirements
trigger_conditions: A process has more than one phase or owner
An invalid transition could bypass review or duplicate side effects
workflow_steps: Define allowed states and terminal outcomes
Specify each transition's event, guard and side effect
Persist state with the evidence that satisfied the guard
Reject invalid or stale transitions
Test recovery, retry and approval-bypass paths
example_prompt: Model this workflow as an explicit state machine. List guarded transitions, persisted evidence and terminal states, then test invalid transitions and recovery without executing side effects.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model draft, review, approved and published states so an edit invalidates approval; this is a design example, not an implemented workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Every transition has an explicit guard and evidence requirement
Invalid, stale and recovery transitions are covered by tests
verification_procedure: Run transition-table fixtures for success, rejection, retry and stale-state cases
security_considerations: Approval and permission checks must be transition guards
Persisted state needs integrity, access control and audit history
fallback_procedure: Use a manual state checklist with recorded transition approvals until a runtime exists.

name: Bounded Retry
description: Retry only classified transient failures under explicit attempt, delay, budget and stop rules.
purpose: Recover from temporary faults without loops, duplicated side effects or hidden cost.
problem_solved: Unbounded retries repeat deterministic failures or duplicate non-idempotent actions.
when_to_use: A failure is plausibly transient
The operation is idempotent or has a deduplication key
when_not_to_use: The failure is deterministic or unauthorized
The action cannot safely be repeated
trigger_conditions: A tool or service returns a retryable timeout or transient status
A retry policy and idempotency guarantee exist
workflow_steps: Classify the failure as transient, deterministic, policy or unknown
Confirm the operation is safe to repeat
Apply the attempt, delay and total-budget limits
Reuse the same idempotency key when required
Stop with a structured failure when the limit or non-retryable class is reached
example_prompt: Decide whether this failure may be retried. Cite the error class and idempotency guarantee, enforce the declared limits and stop immediately on deterministic or policy failures.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: bound retries for a future approved notification delivery using a deduplication key; no notification channel is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Only transient safe failures are retried
Attempt count, delay and total budget are enforced and logged
verification_procedure: Exercise transient, deterministic, unauthorized and repeated-timeout fixtures
Confirm non-idempotent actions are never retried
security_considerations: Retries must not bypass rate limits, approvals or access controls
Backoff must not amplify denial-of-service conditions
fallback_procedure: Stop after the first failure and request human diagnosis when retry safety is unknown.

name: Behaviour-Driven Development
description: Translate business behavior into concrete scenarios, automate those scenarios and implement only what makes them pass.
purpose: Keep implementation tied to shared, business-readable examples of required behavior.
problem_solved: Technical tests pass while stakeholders disagree about the actual business behavior.
when_to_use: Business rules have multiple examples or edge cases
Developers, testers and product owners need a shared specification
when_not_to_use: The change is purely mechanical
No stakeholder can confirm scenario meaning
trigger_conditions: Acceptance criteria contain ambiguous behavior
A rule change needs executable business examples
workflow_steps: Write one behavior as a concrete given-when-then scenario
Add boundary and failure examples with the domain reviewer
Automate the scenarios and confirm the expected failure
Implement the smallest behavior that satisfies them
Review scenario names and evidence against the requirement
example_prompt: Convert this business rule into concrete given-when-then scenarios, including one failure case. Automate them before implementation and keep the language reviewable by a domain owner.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: specify that an expired policy claim cannot enter an eligible digest set, using fixtures rather than a live source.
acceptance_criteria: Scenarios are business-readable and traceable to a requirement
At least one scenario fails before implementation and passes afterward
verification_procedure: Review scenarios with the domain owner
Run the scenario suite before and after the change
security_considerations: Use synthetic examples without personal or confidential data
Scenario approval does not authorize external publication
fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed example table and manual checks until a scenario runner is available.

name: Domain-Driven Design
description: Model complex business behavior with a ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates and explicit domain rules.
purpose: Align code boundaries and terminology with the business domain rather than technical layers alone.
problem_solved: Ambiguous terminology and scattered rules cause inconsistent behavior across modules.
when_to_use: The domain has rich concepts, invariants or multiple subdomains
Business and code terminology repeatedly diverge
when_not_to_use: The application is a simple CRUD wrapper
Domain experts cannot validate the model
trigger_conditions: Business rules span several modules
The same term has different meanings in different contexts
workflow_steps: Extract domain terms and resolve context-specific meanings
Identify bounded contexts and their relationships
Define aggregates, entities, value objects and invariants
Map business rules to model objects and tests
Review the model with a domain owner before changing code boundaries
example_prompt: Model this business domain using a ubiquitous language and bounded contexts. Identify aggregates and invariants, and flag terms whose meaning still needs domain-owner confirmation.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: distinguish source, evidence, claim and event concepts in a proposed model without creating a product database.
acceptance_criteria: Domain terms have context-specific definitions
Every invariant has an owner and a planned verification
verification_procedure: Review the glossary and context map with a domain owner
Trace each invariant to examples and model tests
security_considerations: Domain models must encode authorization and data-classification boundaries
Avoid copying sensitive business records into model examples
fallback_procedure: Start with a glossary and invariant list, then introduce aggregates only where domain complexity justifies them.

name: SOLID Design Principles
description: Review object and module boundaries against single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion.
purpose: Improve changeability and testability without applying principles as automatic abstraction rules.
problem_solved: Classes accumulate unrelated reasons to change or depend on concrete implementations and oversized interfaces.
when_to_use: Designing or reviewing classes, services and module contracts
A change repeatedly forces edits across unrelated responsibilities
when_not_to_use: The code is simple and the abstraction cost exceeds the benefit
No concrete changeability problem has been observed
trigger_conditions: A class or interface has multiple unrelated change drivers
Tests require concrete infrastructure or broad mock interfaces
workflow_steps: List each class or module responsibility and reason to change
Check substitutability and interface breadth at real call sites
Identify concrete dependencies that hinder isolated tests
Propose the smallest boundary change for a confirmed violation
Preserve behavior with characterization and regression tests
example_prompt: Review these boundaries against each SOLID principle using concrete call sites and change drivers. Recommend only the smallest justified refactor and reject speculative abstraction.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: review a proposed evidence-service boundary so storage details do not leak into claim-verification logic.
acceptance_criteria: Each finding cites a concrete responsibility, substitution or dependency problem
Refactoring preserves tested behavior and stays in scope
verification_procedure: Inspect before-and-after interfaces and call sites
Run characterization and regression tests for each boundary change
security_considerations: Abstraction must not hide authorization or validation
Do not broaden interfaces with sensitive operations for convenience
fallback_procedure: Keep the current boundary and record the design concern when no justified, behavior-preserving change is available.

name: Modular Monolith
description: Build one deployable application with enforced module boundaries, explicit contracts and independently testable internal concerns.
purpose: Gain modularity and team ownership without premature distributed-system complexity.
problem_solved: A codebase becomes a tangled monolith or is split into services before boundaries and operational needs are proven.
when_to_use: A new system needs clear modules but simple deployment
Domain boundaries are emerging and service extraction is not justified
when_not_to_use: Independent scaling, deployment or fault isolation is already required
Module boundaries cannot be enforced
trigger_conditions: Cross-module imports are increasing
A team is considering microservices without measured operational need
workflow_steps: Group capabilities by cohesive business responsibility
Define public module contracts and forbidden dependencies
Move shared code to an explicit owner or contract
Add architecture tests or review checks for boundary violations
Record extraction triggers instead of splitting services speculatively
example_prompt: Propose a modular-monolith boundary map for this system. Specify public contracts, forbidden dependencies and measurable triggers that would justify future service extraction.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: keep proposed evidence and digest modules in one deployable boundary until independent scaling is evidenced.
acceptance_criteria: Every module has a public contract and owner
Dependency rules are checked by tests or a documented review gate
verification_procedure: Run architecture dependency checks
Review cross-module call sites and shared-state ownership
security_considerations: Module boundaries must not bypass authorization
Shared databases require explicit schema and access ownership
fallback_procedure: Use package-level boundaries with manual dependency review until architecture tests exist.

name: Dependency Injection
description: Supply collaborators through explicit constructor or factory boundaries instead of constructing concrete dependencies inside business logic.
purpose: Make dependencies visible, replaceable and testable without hidden global state.
problem_solved: Business logic is tightly coupled to infrastructure and difficult to isolate in tests.
when_to_use: A component depends on external services, clocks, storage or configuration
Tests need controlled substitutes
when_not_to_use: A dependency is stable, internal and has no variability
Injection would only add indirection without a test or change need
trigger_conditions: Tests cannot run without live infrastructure
A class directly constructs or locates a collaborator
workflow_steps: Identify collaborators currently created or globally accessed
Define the narrow contract each consumer needs
Inject implementations at an explicit composition root
Test the consumer with controlled fakes
Review lifetimes, disposal and configuration for leaks or hidden state
example_prompt: Refactor these hidden concrete dependencies behind narrow injected contracts. Keep construction at one composition root and prove isolation with fake-based tests.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: inject a fake evidence repository into a future claim-verification component without provisioning a database.
acceptance_criteria: Business logic does not construct infrastructure collaborators
Consumer tests run with controlled substitutes and explicit lifetimes
verification_procedure: Inspect the composition root and dependency graph
Run tests with fakes and verify no live service is required
security_considerations: Do not inject credentials into domain objects or logs
Validate implementations at the composition boundary
fallback_procedure: Introduce a small factory seam first when full constructor injection would exceed the task scope.

name: Strategy Pattern
description: Encapsulate interchangeable algorithms behind one stable contract selected by explicit configuration or context.
purpose: Replace conditional algorithm branches with independently testable implementations.
problem_solved: Growing if/else or switch blocks mix policy selection with algorithm details.
when_to_use: Multiple algorithms satisfy the same contract
Selection varies by source, policy, task or configuration
when_not_to_use: Only one algorithm exists
Variation is speculative or the contract would be unstable
trigger_conditions: A conditional branch selects among processing algorithms
A new algorithm requires edits across unrelated call sites
workflow_steps: Extract the common algorithm contract from real branches
Move each branch into a named strategy
Define deterministic selection and default behavior
Test each strategy against shared contract cases
Add a selection test for unknown and disallowed identifiers
example_prompt: Replace these algorithm branches with explicit strategies behind one contract. Preserve behavior, test each strategy and define safe handling for unknown selections.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: select an approved date-normalization strategy by source format without embedding source-specific conditionals in the domain rule.
acceptance_criteria: Strategies share one tested contract
Selection is deterministic and unknown values fail safely
verification_procedure: Run shared contract cases for every strategy
Compare pre-refactor and post-refactor outputs for representative inputs
security_considerations: Strategy identifiers must not allow arbitrary class loading
Each strategy needs the same validation and authorization expectations
fallback_procedure: Keep the existing branch and add contract tests until a second real algorithm justifies extraction.

name: Repository Pattern
description: Expose persistence operations through a domain-oriented contract while keeping queries, mappings and transactions in an infrastructure implementation.
purpose: Decouple business rules from database APIs and make data access replaceable and testable.
problem_solved: Storage details and queries spread through business logic, causing brittle tests and duplicated persistence rules.
when_to_use: Domain logic depends on durable aggregates or evidence records
Multiple storage implementations or isolated tests are needed
when_not_to_use: The operation is a trivial direct query with no domain behavior
The abstraction would merely rename the database API
trigger_conditions: Business services construct storage calls directly
Data-access concerns hinder isolated domain tests
prerequisites: Fake or disposable storage for tests
workflow_steps: Define persistence needs in domain terms
Specify query, unit-of-work and failure semantics
Implement storage mapping behind the contract
Test the domain with an in-memory or disposable fake
Run integration tests for constraints, transactions and authorization
example_prompt: Define a repository contract for this aggregate without leaking database types. Specify transaction and query semantics, then test both a fake and an approved disposable store.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: isolate a proposed evidence-record repository from a future database choice; no database is created.
acceptance_criteria: Domain code has no storage API dependency
Transaction, query and authorization behavior has contract or integration evidence
verification_procedure: Run domain tests with a fake
Run approved integration fixtures for constraints, rollback and access control
security_considerations: Repository methods must enforce or delegate tenant and role authorization
Avoid generic APIs that expose unrestricted queries or sensitive fields
fallback_procedure: Use a narrow data-access function with domain-language naming until a full repository is justified.

name: Pipeline Pattern
description: Compose ordered processing stages with explicit input/output contracts, validation, failure handling and observability.
purpose: Make multi-stage transformations reusable, testable and easy to diagnose.
problem_solved: Processing logic becomes one opaque function with hidden ordering, mutation and error behavior.
when_to_use: Data passes through repeated transform, validate or enrich stages
Stages need independent tests or replacement
when_not_to_use: The workflow is a single operation
Stages share so much implicit state that contracts would be artificial
trigger_conditions: A function mixes parsing, validation, transformation and output formatting
Failures cannot be attributed to a processing stage
workflow_steps: Define the envelope and provenance carried between stages
Implement one responsibility per stage with schema validation
Specify whether failures stop, skip or quarantine the record
Test each stage and one end-to-end fixture
Record stage versions, timings when measured and failure location
example_prompt: Refactor this processing flow into a staged pipeline. Define envelope contracts, validation and failure policy for each stage, then test stages independently and end to end.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model collect, normalize, extract and verify as separate future stages without enabling collection or model calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every stage has a validated input and output contract
A failing fixture identifies the exact stage and preserves provenance
verification_procedure: Run per-stage unit fixtures and an end-to-end fixture
Inject malformed input at each boundary and inspect failure records
security_considerations: Validate untrusted data at every trust boundary
Do not allow later stages to erase provenance or bypass authorization
fallback_procedure: Use a linear script with explicit checkpoints until reusable stage contracts are proven.

name: Event-Driven Architecture
description: Coordinate producers, event contracts, brokers and consumers with explicit ordering, delivery and failure semantics.
purpose: Decouple asynchronous work while making event ownership and delivery guarantees explicit.
problem_solved: Direct calls couple workflows tightly or events are published without schemas, ordering and replay rules.
when_to_use: Independent consumers react to durable state changes
Asynchronous decoupling or replay is a real requirement
when_not_to_use: A synchronous request/response contract is sufficient
Operational complexity cannot be supported
trigger_conditions: Multiple consumers need the same state-change notification
Temporal coupling blocks independent operation
workflow_steps: Define event meaning, owner and schema version
Map producers, consumers and allowed dependencies
Specify ordering, duplication, retry and dead-letter behavior
Make consumers idempotent and test replay
Document retention, access and operational recovery
example_prompt: Design this event flow with versioned schemas and explicit delivery semantics. Make consumers idempotent, test duplicate and out-of-order events and document replay ownership.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: a future evidence-approved event could trigger draft regeneration; no broker, consumer or publication is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Every event has an owner, version and consumer contract
Duplicate, out-of-order and replay cases have defined behavior and tests
verification_procedure: Run contract tests against a fake broker
Exercise duplicate, reordered, failed and replayed event fixtures
security_considerations: Events must not carry secrets or unauthorized tenant data
Consumers need authorization, replay limits and tamper-evident provenance
fallback_procedure: Use a durable job table or explicit synchronous calls until broker operations are justified.

name: Feature Flags
description: Gate incomplete or risky behavior behind named, owned runtime flags with safe defaults and removal criteria.
purpose: Separate deployment from exposure and provide a controlled rollback path.
problem_solved: Unfinished features become visible on merge or rollback requires a code revert.
when_to_use: A feature needs staged exposure or independent rollout
A reversible kill switch reduces operational risk
when_not_to_use: The change is fully approved and needs no staged exposure
A flag would permanently hide an authorization or correctness rule
trigger_conditions: Code will merge before full user exposure is approved
A high-impact behavior needs a tested disable path
prerequisites: Test matrix for enabled and disabled states
workflow_steps: Name the flag, owner, purpose and safe default
Define targeting and approval rules
Test both flag states and transitions
Record audit events for changes and verify the disable path
Set an expiry or removal criterion
example_prompt: Design a feature flag for this staged change. Specify owner, safe default, targeting, tests for both states, audit events and a removal criterion.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: expose a future digest format to internal review before any public release; no UI or flag service exists.
acceptance_criteria: Both flag states and the disable path are tested
Every flag has an owner, safe default and removal criterion
verification_procedure: Run enabled, disabled and transition-state tests
Inspect flag-change audit records and rollback behavior
security_considerations: Flags must not bypass authorization or consent
Protect flag administration and audit every target change
fallback_procedure: Keep the feature unmerged or disabled in approved configuration until a controlled exposure mechanism exists.

name: Unit Testing
description: Test one isolated behavior or domain rule with controlled dependencies, deterministic fixtures and explicit assertions.
purpose: Localize defects quickly and document fine-grained behavior without infrastructure noise.
problem_solved: Bugs are discovered late in slow integrated flows or units lack precise behavioral coverage.
when_to_use: Implementing functions, classes or domain rules
A defect can be reproduced at a small boundary
when_not_to_use: The behavior only exists across external infrastructure
A test would assert private implementation details rather than behavior
trigger_conditions: A new or changed deterministic behavior exists
A bug has a minimal local reproduction
workflow_steps: Choose one observable behavior and its boundary
Build the smallest deterministic fixture
Assert result, error and relevant side effects
Run the test before and after the change
Review the test for implementation coupling and hidden network access
example_prompt: Add focused unit tests for this behavior using controlled fixtures. Cover one normal case and one boundary or failure case without relying on live services.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: unit-test whether an expired claim is eligible for a future digest using synthetic dates.
acceptance_criteria: Tests are deterministic and isolated from external services
Assertions cover expected results and meaningful failures
verification_procedure: Run the targeted unit suite and inspect failure output
Repeat the tests to detect order dependence or hidden shared state
security_considerations: Use synthetic data and no real secrets
Avoid tests that require production credentials or unrestricted network access
fallback_procedure: Use a small manual assertion script with recorded inputs and outputs if the standard runner is unavailable.

name: Integration Testing
description: Verify interactions between real or realistic components, including contracts, persistence, transactions and failure propagation.
purpose: Detect defects that isolated unit tests cannot expose at module or infrastructure boundaries.
problem_solved: Components pass alone but fail when schemas, transactions, configuration or external services interact.
when_to_use: A change crosses module, database, queue or API boundaries
Contract compatibility and transaction behavior matter
when_not_to_use: No integration boundary exists
A live production system would be mutated
trigger_conditions: Two or more components must cooperate
A unit test uses fakes for the boundary under review
workflow_steps: Identify the exact boundary and contract under test
Start only approved disposable dependencies
Seed minimal fixtures and exercise success plus failure paths
Assert persistence, transaction and error propagation behavior
Clean up state and record environment and component versions
example_prompt: Design integration tests for this component boundary. Use disposable dependencies, verify success and rollback paths and record the exact environment versions.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: verify a proposed repository and schema together on a disposable fixture without creating a production evidence store.
acceptance_criteria: The real boundary is exercised in an isolated environment
Success, failure and cleanup behavior are asserted
verification_procedure: Run the integration suite twice and compare state cleanup
Inspect dependency versions and logs for hidden external calls
security_considerations: Never point integration tests at production data
Use least-privilege test credentials and synthetic records
fallback_procedure: Use contract tests plus a controlled fake and mark full integration verification as incomplete.

name: Regression Testing
description: Select and run tests that demonstrate previously working behavior remains unchanged after a modification.
purpose: Detect unintended side effects before integration or release.
problem_solved: A fix or refactor silently breaks unrelated behavior outside the new test.
when_to_use: Every behavior change, bug fix or structural refactor
A prior defect needs a permanent guard
when_not_to_use: No baseline behavior or test suite exists
A test is flaky or unrelated and cannot be interpreted
trigger_conditions: A diff changes shared code, contracts or data
A previously observed defect is fixed
workflow_steps: Map changed files and contracts to affected behavior
Select existing and new regression cases
Run the targeted set before broader checks
Compare failures with the known-good baseline
Record unrun or flaky checks as unresolved evidence gaps
example_prompt: Select regression tests for this diff based on changed behavior and shared dependencies. Report exact results and do not treat skipped or flaky checks as passing.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: rerun citation and date-validation fixtures after a proposed digest-rule change.
acceptance_criteria: Each material changed behavior has a regression check
Unrun, skipped and flaky checks are explicit
verification_procedure: Compare selected tests with the change-impact map
Inspect command output, exit codes and baseline results
security_considerations: Security-sensitive changes require dedicated security regression cases
Do not weaken assertions to make the suite green
fallback_procedure: Run the full deterministic suite and manually check untested behavior when selection is uncertain.

name: Property-Based Testing
description: State invariants and generate varied inputs to test whether those properties hold across a defined domain.
purpose: Find edge cases that hand-written examples miss while focusing tests on durable behavior.
problem_solved: Tests cover a few examples but fail on unusual valid or boundary inputs.
when_to_use: Inputs have many valid variations
A function has clear invariants such as round-trip, ordering or idempotence
when_not_to_use: The property cannot be stated precisely
Generated cases are too expensive or nondeterministic to interpret
trigger_conditions: Repeated boundary bugs appear
A parser, normalizer or validator accepts a broad input domain
workflow_steps: Write invariants in terms of observable behavior
Define valid generators and explicit domain constraints
Run with a recorded seed and case budget
Shrink each counterexample to a minimal failing input
Add the minimized case as a conventional regression test
example_prompt: Define properties for this function and generate varied valid inputs. Record the seed, shrink failures to minimal counterexamples and convert them into fixed regression cases.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: test that a future date parser preserves the original instant across supported formats and rejects invalid dates.
acceptance_criteria: Properties are precise and independent of implementation details
Counterexamples are minimized, reproducible and retained
verification_procedure: Replay failures with recorded seeds
Review generators for invalid, biased or out-of-domain cases
security_considerations: Generated inputs must not create unsafe file, network or command paths
Bound case counts and input sizes to avoid resource exhaustion
fallback_procedure: Use a curated boundary-case table when no property-testing library is available.

name: Mutation Testing
description: Introduce small, controlled source mutations and check whether the existing test suite detects each one.
purpose: Measure test sensitivity to realistic defects rather than relying only on coverage percentages.
problem_solved: Tests execute many lines but would still pass when important logic is changed or removed.
when_to_use: Critical logic has weak or suspicious tests
Coverage is high but defect escape remains a concern
when_not_to_use: The suite is too slow for bounded mutation runs
Generated mutants cannot be mapped to meaningful behavior
trigger_conditions: A test suite reports high coverage without strong assertions
A defect escaped despite related tests
workflow_steps: Confirm the baseline suite passes
Select a bounded set of meaningful mutation operators
Apply one mutation at a time and run targeted tests
Classify killed, survived, timeout and equivalent mutants
Add tests only for survived mutants that represent observable behavior gaps
example_prompt: Run a bounded mutation analysis on this critical logic. Preserve the baseline, classify every mutant and propose tests only for meaningful surviving behavior gaps.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: mutate a proposed eligibility comparison to see whether future digest tests detect an off-by-one date error.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline tests pass before mutation
Every mutant is classified and meaningful survivors have a test action
verification_procedure: Replay selected killed and survived mutants
Review equivalent-mutant decisions and mutation scope
security_considerations: Mutation runs must use disposable copies
Do not mutate production code, credentials or security controls in place
fallback_procedure: Perform manual fault injection on a disposable copy and record the test response without claiming a mutation score.

name: Differential Testing
description: Run equivalent inputs through two implementations or versions and compare normalized outputs and side effects.
purpose: Detect behavioral divergence during migrations, replacements or performance-oriented rewrites.
problem_solved: A new implementation appears correct on examples but differs subtly from a trusted baseline.
when_to_use: Replacing a parser, algorithm, service or storage layer
Two versions must remain behaviorally compatible
when_not_to_use: The baseline is known to be incorrect without a documented exception
Outputs cannot be normalized meaningfully
trigger_conditions: A parallel implementation or migration is proposed
Unexpected output differences appear between versions
workflow_steps: Freeze the baseline and candidate versions
Define which output and side-effect differences matter
Run the same bounded fixture corpus through both
Normalize irrelevant formatting and classify each divergence
Resolve intended differences through requirements or fix unintended ones
example_prompt: Compare this candidate with the frozen baseline on the shared fixture corpus. Normalize only irrelevant differences and classify every remaining divergence as intended or defective.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: compare old and proposed evidence-normalization rules on synthetic records before a future migration.
acceptance_criteria: Both versions receive identical inputs and environment constraints
Every meaningful divergence is classified with evidence
verification_procedure: Replay reported differences and inspect raw outputs
Check that normalization did not hide semantic or security differences
security_considerations: Use synthetic or approved data for both implementations
Do not route restricted data to an unapproved comparison service
fallback_procedure: Compare a curated fixture table manually and record unresolved equivalence rules.

name: Snapshot Testing
description: Capture a reviewed serialized output baseline and fail on later changes until a human approves the new snapshot.
purpose: Expose unexpected output changes in stable, inspectable artifacts.
problem_solved: Rendered documents, schemas or diagrams change without anyone noticing small but important differences.
when_to_use: Output is deterministic and human-reviewable
Small serialization or rendering changes matter
when_not_to_use: Output contains volatile timestamps or random identifiers without normalization
Reviewers would approve snapshots without inspecting them
trigger_conditions: A generator or renderer produces stable structured output
A prior snapshot diff is unexplained
workflow_steps: Normalize approved volatile fields
Review and store the initial snapshot
Generate the candidate output
Inspect the exact diff and classify intended changes
Update the baseline only with explicit review evidence
example_prompt: Compare this generated output with its reviewed snapshot. Normalize only declared volatile fields, show the exact diff and require review before updating the baseline.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: snapshot a generated diagram description or digest schema while excluding run-specific timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshots are deterministic after declared normalization
Every baseline update has review evidence and a classified diff
verification_procedure: Regenerate output twice and compare stability
Inspect snapshot diffs for hidden semantic changes
security_considerations: Do not store secrets or personal data in snapshots
Treat generated snapshot content as untrusted until reviewed
fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed golden output file and manual diff when no snapshot framework exists.

name: Red Teaming
description: Probe an AI or security-sensitive system with authorized adversarial cases to discover failure modes and control gaps.
purpose: Expose weaknesses that normal acceptance tests and threat models may miss.
problem_solved: Prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool use or policy bypasses remain hidden until adversarial testing.
when_to_use: A system handles untrusted input, model output or privileged tools
A security boundary needs empirical challenge
when_not_to_use: The target or attack scope is not authorized
Testing could affect production, third parties or real users
trigger_conditions: A new AI workflow or trust boundary is proposed
A high-risk control lacks adversarial evidence
prerequisites: Written authorization and rules of engagement
Safe test data and stop conditions
workflow_steps: Confirm authorized scope, target and stop conditions
Derive attack cases from threat hypotheses and trust boundaries
Run cases in isolation with synthetic data
Record reproducible control failures without exploiting unrelated systems
Assign remediation, retest and residual-risk decisions
example_prompt: Design an authorized red-team test plan for these declared threats. Use isolated synthetic targets, define stop conditions and record reproducible findings without claiming exploitation beyond scope.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: test whether malicious article text can influence a future evidence workflow or trigger an unapproved tool call.
acceptance_criteria: Every test maps to an authorized threat hypothesis
Findings include reproduction, impact, control gap and retest criteria
verification_procedure: Replay findings in the isolated environment
Security reviewer checks scope compliance and remediation evidence
security_considerations: No testing against unauthorized or production targets
Protect sensitive findings and avoid storing live secrets in fixtures
fallback_procedure: Use static abuse-case review and mark empirical red-team verification blocked until authorization exists.

name: Failure Injection
description: Introduce controlled dependency failures in an isolated environment and verify detection, retry bounds, recovery and data integrity.
purpose: Demonstrate resilience behavior under faults instead of assuming it from design.
problem_solved: Timeout, partial failure and dependency outage paths are untested and fail unpredictably.
when_to_use: A workflow depends on external services or durable state
Recovery and retry behavior are acceptance requirements
when_not_to_use: Injection would affect production or shared infrastructure
The failure mode cannot be safely isolated
trigger_conditions: A retry, fallback or recovery claim needs evidence
A dependency has known timeout or partial-write failure modes
workflow_steps: Define one fault and the expected system response
Inject it only in an isolated dependency
Observe timeout, retry, fallback and alert behavior
Verify recovery and durable-state integrity
Remove the fault and confirm the system returns to baseline
example_prompt: Inject this declared dependency fault in an isolated test environment. Verify detection, bounded retry, recovery and data integrity, then restore the baseline.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: simulate a future evidence-store timeout during draft generation without touching any live store.
acceptance_criteria: The injected fault is isolated and reversible
Detection, retry limits, recovery and integrity are asserted
verification_procedure: Replay the fault and inspect timing, retry count, recovery and state comparisons
security_considerations: Never inject faults into production or shared systems
Use synthetic data and ensure fault controls cannot escape the test boundary
fallback_procedure: Use fake dependencies that return scripted failures and mark real infrastructure resilience as unverified.

name: Acceptance Test Automation
description: Convert approved acceptance criteria into repeatable, traceable checks with explicit pass, fail and not-run states.
purpose: Make stakeholder acceptance reproducible and tied to exact requirements.
problem_solved: Acceptance depends on memory or manual spot checks and cannot be rerun consistently.
when_to_use: A feature has approved acceptance criteria
A release or task needs repeatable acceptance evidence
when_not_to_use: Criteria are ambiguous or unapproved
The test would require unauthorized production actions
trigger_conditions: A task moves toward completion or release
Acceptance criteria are stable enough to automate
workflow_steps: Assign stable IDs to approved acceptance criteria
Map each criterion to an observable test and fixture
Automate the check with explicit pass and fail conditions
Run in an approved environment and retain exact evidence
Block completion on failure or missing required results
example_prompt: Automate these approved acceptance criteria with traceable IDs and explicit outcomes. Do not infer a pass from skipped tests or unrelated evidence.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: verify that a future digest excludes unsupported claims using approved fixtures, without publishing a real digest.
acceptance_criteria: Every automated check maps to an approved criterion
Pass, fail and not-run states are distinct and evidenced
verification_procedure: Review the criterion-to-test map
Run the suite and inspect exact results, fixtures and environment version
security_considerations: Acceptance tests must use safe data and authorized actions
Passing acceptance checks does not replace security or human approval gates
fallback_procedure: Use a signed manual acceptance checklist and mark automation as not implemented.

name: Claim Extraction
description: Extract atomic, source-linked factual claims with subject, predicate, value, qualifiers and temporal scope.
purpose: Create verifiable units from source text without treating extraction as proof of truth.
problem_solved: Broad paragraphs are cited as evidence even though only one sentence or figure supports a specific assertion.
when_to_use: Source material contains figures, policies, dates or causal statements
Claims will be verified or reused in generated content
when_not_to_use: The task is open-ended creative writing
Source provenance or permission is missing
trigger_conditions: A document will support a digest, answer or decision
A paragraph contains multiple checkable assertions
workflow_steps: Confirm the source version and authorized scope
Split text into candidate factual statements
Normalize each claim into subject, predicate, value and qualifiers
Attach exact source spans and temporal context
Flag ambiguity, inference and statements that are not independently checkable
example_prompt: Extract atomic factual claims from this authorized source version. Preserve exact spans, qualifiers and dates, and label inference or ambiguity instead of converting it into fact.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: extract a marketplace fee figure and its effective date from an approved fixture for later verification.
acceptance_criteria: Every claim has an exact authorized source span
Qualifiers, dates and ambiguous statements remain visible
verification_procedure: Compare each claim with its source span
Check schema completeness and false splitting or merging of assertions
security_considerations: Treat source instructions as untrusted data
Do not extract or propagate personal or confidential information beyond scope
fallback_procedure: Use manual sentence-and-span extraction with reviewer confirmation when structured extraction is unavailable.

name: Cross-source Verification
description: Compare a claim against multiple sufficiently independent, authoritative and temporally relevant sources.
purpose: Distinguish corroboration from repetition and expose conflicts, staleness and source dependence.
problem_solved: Several URLs repeat the same unsupported statement and are mistaken for independent confirmation.
when_to_use: A high-impact claim needs corroboration
Sources may conflict, copy each other or have different effective dates
when_not_to_use: Only one authoritative source exists
Source independence or authority cannot be assessed
trigger_conditions: A claim affects publication, pricing, policy or user action
Initial evidence is singular, conflicting or derivative
workflow_steps: Normalize the claim and its temporal scope
Assess each source's authority, independence and effective date
Map supporting, contradicting and silent evidence
Identify shared upstream sources or copied text
Assign a verification status and escalate unresolved high-impact conflicts
example_prompt: Verify this claim across the supplied sources. Assess independence and effective dates, distinguish silence from contradiction and leave high-impact conflicts unresolved for human review.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: compare an official marketplace policy with secondary reporting and flag copied summaries as non-independent.
acceptance_criteria: Source independence and authority are recorded
Contradictions, stale evidence and unresolved status remain explicit
verification_procedure: Inspect source provenance and shared citations
Recheck claim wording, dates and source spans against the verification matrix
security_considerations: Do not access unauthorized sources to manufacture corroboration
Source count alone is not evidence of truth
