fallback_procedure: Mark the claim unresolved and request an authoritative source rather than inferring support from weak evidence.

name: Entity Resolution
description: Determine whether records refer to the same real-world entity using identifiers, attributes, context and explicit merge rules.
purpose: Unify duplicate entity references without collapsing distinct people, products, sources or events.
problem_solved: Name variation creates duplicate records while aggressive matching merges unrelated entities.
when_to_use: Records use inconsistent names, aliases or identifiers
Entity identity affects evidence, counting or personalization
when_not_to_use: No stable identity evidence exists
A false merge would create material harm
trigger_conditions: Duplicate entity candidates are detected
Cross-source records need a canonical identity link
workflow_steps: Normalize candidate identifiers and names without destroying originals
Compare stable identifiers, aliases and contextual attributes
Apply explicit match, non-match and review rules
Record evidence for every merge or split decision
Test ambiguous and adversarial near-match fixtures
example_prompt: Resolve whether these records represent the same entity. Preserve original identifiers, cite match evidence and route ambiguous near-matches to review instead of forcing a merge.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: link marketplace and policy-source records that refer to the same platform while keeping distinct regional entities separate.
acceptance_criteria: Every merge has evidence and a reversible decision record
Ambiguous and near-match cases are not automatically merged
verification_procedure: Review a labeled sample of matches and non-matches
security_considerations: Do not merge identities using sensitive attributes without authorization
Preserve provenance and provide correction or split procedures
fallback_procedure: Keep records separate with candidate links until a reviewer can resolve identity.

name: Event Clustering
description: Group source reports into real-world events using shared entities, time windows, locations and factual overlap while preserving distinct incidents.
purpose: Consolidate coverage of the same event without merging unrelated or repeated developments.
problem_solved: Duplicate news reports inflate event counts or separate reports fragment one developing story.
when_to_use: Multiple sources report related developments
Event-level evidence, counts or timelines are needed
when_not_to_use: Reports are too sparse to establish a shared event
Similar wording is the only available signal
trigger_conditions: Candidate reports share entities, dates or claims
A digest needs one event record with multiple sources
workflow_steps: Normalize report dates, entities and locations
Generate candidate groups using factual and temporal overlap
Distinguish the same event from recurring or related incidents
Preserve every member source and contradictory claim
Review borderline clusters and record split or merge decisions
example_prompt: Cluster these reports by real-world event, not wording alone. Preserve source links and contradictions, and flag recurring or related incidents that must remain separate.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: group several approved reports about one policy change while keeping a later reversal as a distinct event.
acceptance_criteria: Each cluster has an event rationale and complete member provenance
Related but distinct incidents remain separate
verification_procedure: Review boundary and recurring-event fixtures
Compare cluster membership with entity, date and claim evidence
security_considerations: Clustering must not amplify unverified claims
Avoid inferring sensitive identities or locations from weak matches
fallback_procedure: Use a manually reviewed event timeline and leave uncertain reports unclustered.

name: Temporal Reasoning
description: Reason explicitly about publication, event, effective, expiry and observation times, including time zones and unknown dates.
purpose: Prevent current, historical and future claims from being treated as simultaneously valid.
problem_solved: Evidence is cited without accounting for when it was published, effective or superseded.
when_to_use: Policies, prices, schedules or events change over time
A claim's validity depends on an effective interval
when_not_to_use: The claim has no temporal dimension
Dates are unavailable and cannot be marked unknown
trigger_conditions: A source contains multiple date types
A digest or decision requires current-as-of reasoning
workflow_steps: Classify each date as publication, event, effective, expiry or observation time
Normalize time zones and preserve original date text
Compare intervals against the declared as-of time
Flag unknown, contradictory and superseded dates
Require revalidation when the reference time or source version changes
example_prompt: Analyze the temporal validity of these claims as of the stated time. Separate publication from effective dates, preserve unknowns and flag superseded or contradictory intervals.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: distinguish a policy announcement date from its effective date before a future seller digest uses the claim.
acceptance_criteria: Date types and time zones are explicit
Unknown and conflicting dates are not silently resolved
verification_procedure: Check boundary fixtures for start, end, expiry and time-zone changes
Recompute validity at a different as-of time
security_considerations: Do not infer consent or applicability from ambiguous dates
Preserve original date evidence for audit
fallback_procedure: Mark temporal validity unresolved and request source clarification instead of assuming the publication date is effective.

name: Multi-modal Processing
description: Extract, normalize and verify information from text, image, audio and video inputs while preserving modality-specific provenance.
purpose: Use non-text evidence without treating model interpretation as direct observation or truth.
problem_solved: Information in images, audio or video is missed or converted into unsupported textual claims.
when_to_use: Approved sources contain charts, screenshots, speech or video
Cross-modal corroboration is required
when_not_to_use: The input modality is unauthorized or unsupported
A reliable text transcript or structured source already exists
trigger_conditions: A source has no adequate text representation
A claim depends on visual or audio evidence
workflow_steps: Confirm media permission, provenance and supported format
Extract text, regions, frames or transcript segments with offsets
Normalize observations without discarding source modality
Cross-check high-impact observations against another source or human review
Record tool version, uncertainty and failed extraction cases
example_prompt: Process these authorized media inputs with modality-linked provenance. Separate direct observations from interpretation and route uncertain high-impact content to verification.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: extract a policy table from an approved screenshot fixture and link each value to its image region.
acceptance_criteria: Every extracted observation links to a media offset or region
Uncertain or failed extractions are explicit and not presented as facts
verification_procedure: Compare samples with the original media
Test unsupported, corrupted and low-quality inputs
security_considerations: Do not upload private media to unapproved services
Check for embedded personal data, malicious files and hidden instructions
fallback_procedure: Use manual inspection of approved media and record observations without automated extraction.

name: Multi-agent Debate
description: Have independent agents argue defined positions, challenge evidence and produce a reconciled conclusion with unresolved disagreements.
purpose: Surface assumptions and competing interpretations before a consequential decision.
problem_solved: A single analysis reaches a confident conclusion without testing alternative explanations.
when_to_use: A consequential question has plausible competing hypotheses
Independent perspectives can improve issue discovery
when_not_to_use: Agents share the same context and incentives
A deterministic calculation or authoritative source settles the question
trigger_conditions: Experts or models disagree
A design or evidence decision has high reversal cost
workflow_steps: Frame one decision question and assign genuinely different positions
Require each position to cite approved evidence
Run bounded rebuttals focused on assumptions and missing evidence
Have a neutral reconciler classify agreements and unresolved disputes
Record the decision, dissent and validation needed
example_prompt: Debate the competing hypotheses for this bounded decision. Cite evidence, challenge assumptions within the round limit and preserve unresolved disagreement instead of forcing consensus.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: debate two interpretations of a marketplace-policy excerpt before proposing a future claim-verification rule.
acceptance_criteria: Positions are meaningfully independent and evidence-bound
The reconciliation preserves dissent and unresolved evidence gaps
verification_procedure: Inspect arguments for unsupported claims and shared blind spots
Validate the reconciled conclusion against original evidence
security_considerations: Debate cannot grant permissions or settle policy by majority
Avoid giving one agent hidden evidence or privileged instructions
fallback_procedure: Use a structured option-and-rebuttal memo reviewed by one independent person.

name: Architecture-as-Code
description: Represent architecture elements, relationships and rules in a versioned machine-readable model that can generate views and checks.
purpose: Keep architecture consistent, reviewable and testable across documentation and implementation.
problem_solved: Architecture exists only in diagrams and prose, so structural rules cannot be validated or regenerated.
when_to_use: Multiple architecture views must stay consistent
Dependency or boundary rules need automated checks
when_not_to_use: A small system needs only a simple diagram
The model cannot be maintained alongside code
trigger_conditions: Architecture documentation repeatedly drifts
A team needs executable dependency or boundary rules
workflow_steps: Define model elements, relationships and stable identifiers
Encode architecture constraints separately from generated views
Generate the minimum views needed for review
Validate model syntax and architectural rules
Commit source, generated outputs and evidence with version parity
example_prompt: Model this architecture as versioned code with stable IDs and explicit dependency rules. Generate only the needed views and report validation separately from rendering.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: represent proposed Ecomdy module boundaries in a model while keeping DevHarness outside the product runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Model and generated views share one versioned source
Architecture constraints have machine or documented review checks
verification_procedure: Regenerate views and compare source parity
Run constraint fixtures for allowed and forbidden dependencies
security_considerations: Do not expose sensitive infrastructure details in generated public views
Treat generated files as derived artifacts, not independent authority
fallback_procedure: Use a structured YAML or JSON inventory with manual view generation until a modeling tool is approved.

name: Architecture Drift Detection
description: Compare observed code, dependencies, deployment and data flows with the approved architecture model and classify differences.
purpose: Detect undocumented architectural change before it undermines assumptions or controls.
problem_solved: Documentation describes intended structure while the implemented system quietly violates it.
when_to_use: Architecture rules exist and implementation evolves
A review needs evidence of structural conformance
when_not_to_use: No approved architecture baseline exists
Observed state cannot be inspected safely
trigger_conditions: A dependency, module, deployment or data flow changes
Generated architecture checks report a mismatch
workflow_steps: Freeze the approved architecture version
Extract observed components, dependencies and interfaces
Compare structure using stable identifiers
Classify each difference as violation, intentional evolution or unknown
Assign remediation or an architecture-decision update with review
example_prompt: Compare observed dependencies and interfaces with this approved architecture model. Classify every difference and require review before changing either the code or the baseline.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: detect whether a proposed module begins depending directly on another module's storage implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Every reported difference cites observed and expected structure
Unknown differences are not silently accepted
verification_procedure: Reproduce extraction and compare stable IDs
Review false positives and intentional architecture decisions
security_considerations: Architecture scans must avoid secret-bearing files and private systems
Drift findings require review before automated remediation
fallback_procedure: Perform a manual dependency and documentation comparison and mark coverage limitations.

name: Data Flow Modeling
description: Model how data enters, moves, transforms, persists and leaves a system with sources, sinks, stores and trust boundaries.
purpose: Make data handling, ownership and security boundaries explicit before implementation.
problem_solved: Teams understand components but not where sensitive data travels or which process transforms it.
when_to_use: Designing data pipelines or integrations
Threat modeling, privacy review or provenance design
when_not_to_use: No data crosses a meaningful boundary
A simple sequence diagram communicates the same flow
trigger_conditions: A new source, store, processor or export is proposed
Data classification or retention is unclear
workflow_steps: Identify data elements and classification
Map sources, processors, stores and sinks
Annotate transformations, ownership and retention
Draw trust and permission boundaries
Validate the model against requirements and threat cases
example_prompt: Model this data flow from source to sink. Label classification, transformations, stores, retention and trust boundaries, and identify unapproved paths.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: map an approved source fixture through normalization and claim verification to a draft without enabling live collection.
acceptance_criteria: Every data path has a source, destination and owner
Trust, classification and retention boundaries are explicit
verification_procedure: Walk each path against actual contracts and fixtures
Security reviewer checks boundary crossings and unapproved sinks
security_considerations: Do not omit sensitive or failure paths from the model
External sinks require explicit data-handling approval
fallback_procedure: Use a structured source-process-store-sink table if diagram tooling is unavailable.

name: Sequence Modeling
description: Model ordered interactions among actors and components, including alternatives, errors, timeouts and retries.
purpose: Clarify runtime behavior and handoffs that structural architecture views do not show.
problem_solved: Teams implement the right components in the wrong order or miss failure and timeout paths.
when_to_use: A workflow crosses multiple actors or services
Ordering, authorization or retry behavior is consequential
when_not_to_use: The interaction is a single synchronous call
A state model better represents the behavior
trigger_conditions: A new API or workflow is designed
A defect involves ordering, timeout or handoff
workflow_steps: Choose one use case and define participants
List ordered messages with preconditions and responses
Add timeout, error, retry and cancellation alternatives
Check authorization and idempotency at each call
Validate the model against contracts and test cases
example_prompt: Model this interaction sequence with success, timeout and retry alternatives. Show preconditions, responses and idempotency boundaries instead of only drawing the happy path.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model a future review request where an edited draft invalidates approval and requires a new review.
acceptance_criteria: Ordering and alternatives are explicit
Each call has a contract, failure behavior and relevant security check
verification_procedure: Trace the model against API contracts and fixtures
Review timeout, retry and cancellation paths with implementers
security_considerations: Do not expose secrets or tokens in sequence artifacts
Authorization checks must occur at the correct boundary
fallback_procedure: Use a numbered interaction table with alternatives and failure handling.

name: ERD Modeling
description: Model entities, keys, relationships, cardinality, constraints and ownership for a persistent data design.
purpose: Make data structure and integrity rules reviewable before schema implementation or migration.
problem_solved: Schemas accumulate ambiguous relationships, duplicated facts and missing integrity constraints.
when_to_use: Designing or changing a persistent schema
Reviewing migration impact and data ownership
when_not_to_use: No durable relational data is involved
The schema is trivial and already fully specified
trigger_conditions: New entities or relationships are proposed
A migration changes keys, cardinality or constraints
workflow_steps: Define entities, stable keys and ownership
Specify relationships and cardinality from business rules
Add uniqueness, nullability and integrity constraints
Check normalization against actual query and update needs
Validate the model with migration and access-control fixtures
example_prompt: Create an ERD for this bounded data model. Specify keys, cardinality and integrity constraints, and identify ownership or normalization questions that need review before migration.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: model source, evidence and claim relationships for a proposed store without creating a database.
acceptance_criteria: Every relationship has cardinality and ownership
Integrity constraints map to business rules and migration checks
verification_procedure: Review valid and invalid relationship fixtures
Compare the ERD with migration SQL or schema definitions
security_considerations: Classify sensitive attributes and minimize stored data
ERDs must not expose real records or credentials
fallback_procedure: Use a table of entities, keys and relationships if a visual ERD cannot be rendered.

name: Design Tokens
description: Define shared semantic values for color, typography, spacing, motion and diagram styling with named usage rules.
purpose: Keep UI and visual documentation consistent without scattering raw design values.
problem_solved: Components and diagrams drift in styling and redesigns require broad manual edits.
when_to_use: A design system or multiple visual surfaces exist
Teams need consistent accessible and brand-approved styles
when_not_to_use: A single static artifact needs no reuse
Token semantics would be invented without design authority
trigger_conditions: Repeated raw values appear across components or diagrams
A visual redesign or accessibility correction needs coordinated change
workflow_steps: Inventory repeated visual values and their purposes
Define semantic token names rather than raw-value aliases
Specify allowed usage, fallback and deprecation behavior
Apply tokens to representative components or diagrams
Validate contrast, consistency and migration coverage
example_prompt: Create semantic design tokens for these repeated visual values. Include usage constraints and accessibility checks, and do not encode unapproved brand choices.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: align a future editorial dashboard and diagram palette through shared semantic tokens; no UI is implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Tokens have semantic names and explicit usage rules
Representative visuals use tokens and pass contrast checks
verification_procedure: Search for remaining raw values in scoped assets
Compare rendered samples and accessibility results
security_considerations: Do not embed tenant data or secrets in token definitions
Review generated assets for unsafe external resources
fallback_procedure: Use a small reviewed style constants file until a full token system is justified.

name: Screenshot-Driven Development
description: Translate an approved reference screenshot into explicit layout, content, state and responsive requirements before implementation.
purpose: Reduce visual guesswork while preserving accessibility and behavior beyond pixel imitation.
problem_solved: Developers infer spacing, states and responsive behavior from an image and miss design intent.
when_to_use: An approved visual reference exists
A UI change must match a reviewed design
when_not_to_use: The screenshot is unapproved, stale or contains sensitive data
No runnable UI or design specification exists
trigger_conditions: A design handoff consists mainly of screenshots
Visual parity needs a reviewable implementation target
workflow_steps: Confirm screenshot version, scope and viewport
Extract layout hierarchy, spacing, content and visible states
Identify missing responsive, loading, error and accessibility requirements
Implement the smallest component set against the specification
Compare in a browser and record intentional deviations
example_prompt: Turn this approved screenshot into a layout and state specification. Identify missing responsive and accessibility behavior before implementing, then compare the result in a browser.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: implement a future digest-review mockup from an approved fixture without treating the screenshot as an approved product requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation traces to a versioned visual specification
Responsive, error and accessibility behavior is checked beyond pixel parity
verification_procedure: Compare scoped viewports in an approved browser
Review accessibility and intentional deviation records
security_considerations: Redact sensitive data in screenshots and traces
Do not fetch remote design assets without approval
fallback_procedure: Use a written layout and state checklist when browser or screenshot tooling is unavailable.

name: Living Documentation
description: Update authoritative documentation in the same change as code, contracts or architecture, with ownership and freshness checks.
purpose: Keep documentation trustworthy and useful instead of allowing it to decay after implementation.
problem_solved: Documentation describes obsolete behavior and cannot be tied to the current version.
when_to_use: A change alters behavior, setup, APIs, architecture or operations
Documentation is part of the definition of done
when_not_to_use: No user or maintainer-facing behavior changed
A change is still an unapproved proposal
trigger_conditions: A PR changes code or contracts
A validation or review finds stale instructions
workflow_steps: Identify which authoritative documents the change affects
Update behavior, examples and limitations in the same task
Mark target design separately from observed as-built state
Run link, terminology and documentation validators
Assign an owner and review trigger for time-sensitive content
example_prompt: Update the authoritative documentation affected by this change. Preserve target-versus-as-built distinctions, validate links and record any content that still needs owner review.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: document a future citation-rule change alongside its tests while keeping proposed Ecomdy behavior clearly labeled.
acceptance_criteria: Every material behavior change has a documentation delta
Documentation distinguishes verified state from proposals and passes validation
verification_procedure: Compare the diff with documentation changes
Run validators and sample instructions against the current implementation
security_considerations: Do not publish secrets, private source text or unsupported capability claims
Generated documentation requires source and freshness checks
fallback_procedure: Add a bounded change note and owner follow-up when the authoritative document cannot be updated safely in the same task.

name: Short-lived Branches
description: Keep issue branches narrowly scoped, frequently synchronized and merged or closed within an explicit age limit.
purpose: Reduce merge debt, stale diffs and hidden long-running divergence.
problem_solved: Large or abandoned branches accumulate conflicts and bypass timely review.
when_to_use: Work is tracked by discrete issues or task contracts
Shared-branch integration is protected by review
when_not_to_use: A long-running release branch is explicitly required
The branch has no bounded objective or owner
trigger_conditions: A new issue enters implementation
A branch exceeds its age, size or synchronization threshold
workflow_steps: Create a branch from the approved current base with a task ID
Limit the diff to the task contract
Sync or rebase only through the approved safe procedure
Review age, size and conflict indicators
Merge, split or close the branch before limits are exceeded
example_prompt: Assess this issue branch against scope, age, size and base-branch freshness. Recommend merge, split, sync or closure without rewriting shared history.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: keep a technique-card update on a small issue branch and avoid unrelated registry changes.
acceptance_criteria: Branch maps to one bounded task
Age, size and freshness limits are checked before merge
verification_procedure: Inspect branch ancestry, diff and task mapping
Compare base and branch heads for stale or unrelated changes
security_considerations: Do not force-push shared branches or bypass review
Branch names and logs must not contain secrets
fallback_procedure: Keep work local and unmerged until it can be split into a reviewable branch.

name: Trunk-Based Development
description: Integrate small reviewed changes frequently into a shared trunk while using short branches or feature flags for incomplete exposure.
purpose: Minimize long-lived divergence and keep integration risk continuously visible.
problem_solved: Infrequent large merges hide conflicts, regressions and incomplete integration.
when_to_use: The team has reliable CI and review gates
Changes can be kept small and safely disabled until ready
when_not_to_use: CI or review is unreliable
A release train requires a separately approved long-lived branch
trigger_conditions: Integration delays or merge conflicts are increasing
A branch approaches the short-lived limit
workflow_steps: Split work into the smallest reviewable increments
Require passing checks and independent review before integration
Merge to trunk frequently within the approved cadence
Use controlled flags for incomplete user exposure
Monitor integration failures and rollback or pause when thresholds are exceeded
example_prompt: Assess this change for frequent trunk integration. Split oversized scope, require current checks and review, and use a controlled flag rather than a long-lived branch when exposure must be delayed.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: integrate small advisory harness changes frequently while keeping product features unimplemented.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated increments are small, reviewed and green
Incomplete exposure is controlled without bypassing trunk protections
verification_procedure: Inspect merge cadence, branch age and CI results
Review rollback and feature-flag evidence for incomplete work
security_considerations: Trunk-based development never authorizes direct pushes or skipped review
Protect required checks and avoid force-pushing shared history
fallback_procedure: Use short-lived branches with serialized merges until CI reliability supports frequent integration.

name: Scope Guard
description: Compare every proposed or observed change with the task's allowed paths, contracts and non-goals before accepting it.
purpose: Detect and stop scope expansion, unrelated cleanup and unauthorized file changes.
problem_solved: Agents modify convenient but out-of-scope files or hide extra changes inside a larger task.
when_to_use: Every mutating task
Reviewing generated patches or multi-agent output
when_not_to_use: No mutation is proposed
The task contract lacks an explicit scope
trigger_conditions: A diff or plan includes a new path or contract
A requested action exceeds declared non-goals
workflow_steps: Load the approved task scope and non-goals
List every changed or proposed path and contract
Classify each change as required, dependent or unrelated
Block unrelated changes and request approval for necessary expansion
Recheck scope after each execution or generation step
example_prompt: Check this diff against the approved task contract. Identify every out-of-scope path or contract change and stop unrelated edits rather than folding them into the task.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: prevent a technique-card data update from modifying the main technique registry or schema.
acceptance_criteria: Every changed path has a scope rationale
Unrelated changes are blocked or separately approved
verification_procedure: Compare Git diff and generated-file inventory with allowed paths
Review dependency-related exceptions with the task owner
security_considerations: Scope checks complement but do not replace filesystem permissions
Never treat an agent's own scope expansion as approval
fallback_procedure: Use a manual changed-path checklist and stop when scope cannot be established.

name: Least Privilege
description: Grant each agent, tool, credential and runtime only the permissions required for the approved task and duration.
purpose: Limit the blast radius of mistakes, prompt injection and compromised components.
problem_solved: Broad credentials and tool permissions allow unrelated reads, writes, network access or paid actions.
when_to_use: Provisioning agents, tools, service accounts or CI runners
Reviewing permission changes
when_not_to_use: No privileged capability is needed
Permissions cannot be mapped to a task requirement
trigger_conditions: A new tool, connector or credential is proposed
A role requests broader access than its task requires
workflow_steps: List the exact actions and resources required by the task
Map each action to the narrowest role, tool and credential
Separate read, write, network, paid and administrative capabilities
Test allowed and denied actions with safe fixtures
Set expiry, rotation, revocation and periodic review
example_prompt: Derive a least-privilege permission matrix for this task. Deny capabilities that are not required and define expiry, rotation and revocation before access is granted.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: give a future evidence reviewer read-only access to approved records without publication or source-management rights.
acceptance_criteria: Every permission maps to a required action
Denied actions and credential lifecycle controls are tested and documented
verification_procedure: Run allowed and denied permission fixtures
Review credential scope, expiry and revocation evidence
security_considerations: Never share administrator credentials or place them in prompts
Local policy cannot replace host and cloud access controls
fallback_procedure: Deny the capability and use a human-mediated action until narrow access can be verified.

name: Pre-commit Hooks
description: Run fast, deterministic formatting, schema, secret and scope checks before a commit is created.
purpose: Catch local defects early while keeping commits reviewable and free of obvious policy violations.
problem_solved: Developers discover formatting, schema or secret issues only after push or CI.
when_to_use: Checks are fast, local and deterministic
The repository has an approved hook mechanism
when_not_to_use: A hook requires network, paid services or unbounded execution
The hook would silently modify unrelated files
trigger_conditions: A commit is about to be created
A repeated local defect should be prevented
workflow_steps: Inspect only staged content and declared checks
Run bounded local validators without network access
Report exact findings and leave unrelated files untouched
Block the commit on material failures
Verify hook version and any approved bypass record
example_prompt: Design pre-commit checks for this staged diff using fast local validators. Block on schema, secret or scope failures and do not modify unrelated files or require network access.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: run a future technique-schema check on staged catalogue data without changing the main registry.
acceptance_criteria: Hooks are deterministic, bounded and scoped to staged changes
Failures block the commit with exact findings
verification_procedure: Test clean, malformed, secret-bearing and over-limit staged fixtures
Inspect hook configuration and approved bypass records
security_considerations: Hooks are convenience controls and can be bypassed
Do not execute unreviewed hook code or log secrets
fallback_procedure: Run the same checks manually on staged content and record the results before committing.

name: Policy-as-Code
description: Express approved organizational or security rules as versioned, testable checks with explicit enforcement and exception handling.
purpose: Make policy consistent, reviewable and auditable across repositories and automation.
problem_solved: Rules live only in prose and are applied inconsistently or cannot be tested before enforcement.
when_to_use: A rule is stable, authoritative and machine-checkable
Multiple repositories or pipelines need consistent enforcement
when_not_to_use: The policy is ambiguous or still proposed
A check would encode an unapproved interpretation
trigger_conditions: A policy repeatedly causes review debate
A new CI, deployment or access rule is approved
workflow_steps: Translate one approved rule into a testable assertion
Define inputs, severity and enforcement point
Add compliant, violating and exception fixtures
Run checks in advisory mode before blocking
Version rule changes and audit every exception with an owner and expiry
example_prompt: Convert this approved policy into a testable rule. Define severity, enforcement and exception handling, and validate compliant and violating fixtures before enabling blocking behavior.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: encode a future requirement that published digest claims must cite authorized evidence, without claiming enforcement exists.
acceptance_criteria: Every rule traces to an approved policy source
Compliant, violating and expired-exception cases are tested
verification_procedure: Run policy fixtures and inspect enforcement logs
Review rule changes and exception records with the policy owner
security_considerations: Policy code is security-sensitive and requires review
Exceptions must be narrow, time-bound and auditable
fallback_procedure: Use a reviewed manual policy checklist and record gaps until rules can be safely encoded.

name: Scheduled Automation
description: Run approved recurring jobs on an explicit schedule with idempotency, overlap prevention, budgets, logging and pause controls.
purpose: Automate periodic work without duplicate runs, silent drift or uncontrolled resource use.
problem_solved: Scheduled jobs overlap, retry indefinitely, use stale configuration or continue after failures.
when_to_use: A task has a genuine time-based cadence
The job is idempotent and has an operational owner
when_not_to_use: An event trigger is more appropriate
No approval, monitoring or pause mechanism exists
trigger_conditions: A recurring requirement has an approved cadence
A manual periodic task causes delays or omissions
workflow_steps: Confirm cadence, time zone and operational owner
Make the job idempotent and prevent overlapping runs
Apply source, runtime, cost and retry limits
Log run IDs, outcomes and freshness without secrets
Test pause, resume, missed-run and failure behavior
example_prompt: Design this recurring job with an explicit schedule, overlap lock and budget. Define idempotency, logging, alerting and pause behavior before enabling any automation.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: plan a future approved source-check schedule; no crawler or scheduler is activated.
acceptance_criteria: Schedule, owner and time zone are explicit
Overlap, retry, budget and pause behavior is tested
verification_procedure: Simulate on-time, overlapping, missed and failed runs
Inspect run logs, freshness and pause controls
security_considerations: Scheduled credentials need least privilege and rotation
No job may expand source access or publication authority automatically
fallback_procedure: Use a human-run checklist with recorded cadence until scheduling controls are approved.

name: Event-driven Automation
description: Trigger bounded automation from authenticated events with schema validation, deduplication, authorization and replay controls.
purpose: Respond to approved system events without trusting payloads or creating duplicate side effects.
problem_solved: Webhook or event handlers act on spoofed, malformed or duplicate events and repeat mutations.
when_to_use: An approved external or internal event should start a workflow
Event authenticity and idempotency can be verified
when_not_to_use: The event source is unauthenticated
A periodic schedule is the correct trigger
trigger_conditions: A supported event occurs
An event schema and authorization policy exist
workflow_steps: Authenticate the event source and validate the payload schema
Authorize the requested action against policy
Deduplicate using an event ID or idempotency key
Run the bounded workflow and record its outcome
Handle replay, ordering and malformed-event cases safely
example_prompt: Design an event-triggered automation contract. Authenticate and validate events, authorize actions, deduplicate side effects and define replay and malformed-event handling.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: a future approved review event could invalidate a digest approval; no Jira, GitHub or product event handler is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated, malformed and unauthorized events are rejected
Duplicate and replayed events do not duplicate side effects
verification_procedure: Exercise valid, spoofed, duplicate, reordered and malformed fixtures
Inspect authorization, deduplication and audit records
security_considerations: Event payloads are untrusted and may contain injection text
Verify signatures, replay windows and least-privilege actions
fallback_procedure: Queue the event for manual review when authenticity or idempotency cannot be established.

name: Budget Enforcement
description: Set and enforce hard limits for iterations, runtime, tokens, tool calls, network use and paid spend before and during execution.
purpose: Prevent runaway work, surprise cost and resource exhaustion with explicit stop behavior.
problem_solved: Tasks continue after their useful limit or exceed approved operational cost without a reliable stop.
when_to_use: Agent loops, batch jobs or paid services are used
A task has a declared resource ceiling
when_not_to_use: The action is a single bounded local operation
No reliable counter or stop mechanism exists
trigger_conditions: A task starts with resource limits
Observed usage approaches a configured threshold
workflow_steps: Define hard and warning limits for each resource
Choose counters that fail closed when usage is unknown
Check limits before each iteration or external call
Stop, checkpoint or escalate at the declared threshold
Record observed usage separately from estimates and unmeasured values
example_prompt: Enforce the declared task budgets before and during execution. Stop at hard limits, record observed usage and mark unknown token or cost values instead of estimating them as facts.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: cap a future batch evidence review by records and runtime without enabling paid model calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every hard limit has a tested stop action
Observed, estimated and unknown usage are clearly separated
verification_procedure: Test below-limit, warning, hard-limit and counter-failure fixtures
Inspect stop timing and checkpoint or escalation records
security_considerations: Budget controls must not be bypassable by retries or child jobs
Cost limits do not replace data or permission controls
fallback_procedure: Reduce task scope to one bounded step and stop if usage cannot be measured reliably.

name: Reproducible Environments
description: Define and verify toolchain, dependency, configuration and data setup so a clean environment produces equivalent results.
purpose: Remove hidden machine state and make setup, tests and evidence repeatable across developers and CI.
problem_solved: A task passes on one machine but fails elsewhere because of unpinned tools, implicit configuration or stale state.
when_to_use: Onboarding, CI or release preparation
Test failures may depend on local environment drift
when_not_to_use: The task has no executable environment
Reproduction would require copying secrets or private production data
trigger_conditions: A clean clone is set up
Results differ across machines or runners
workflow_steps: Inventory required runtimes, tools and dependencies
Pin versions, sources and configuration schemas
Create a clean environment without inherited user state
Run the declared setup and verification commands
Compare outputs and record platform-specific differences
example_prompt: Define a clean reproducible environment for this repository. Pin approved versions and sources, exclude secrets and verify setup from an empty workspace rather than relying on local caches.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: reproduce advisory harness validators in a clean container using only repository-declared dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Environment inputs are versioned and secret-free
A clean setup reaches the same declared verification results
verification_procedure: Repeat setup in a clean environment and compare command outputs
Inspect lockfiles, tool versions and excluded local state
security_considerations: Verify dependency sources and hashes
Do not bake credentials or private data into images or setup scripts
fallback_procedure: Record exact tool versions and manual setup steps, and mark environment reproducibility as incomplete.

name: Continuous Integration
description: Automatically build and verify every proposed integration with deterministic checks, required status reporting and protected merge gates.
purpose: Detect integration defects early and make merge readiness depend on current evidence.
problem_solved: Changes merge without repeatable build, test, schema, security or scope verification.
when_to_use: A shared repository has multiple contributors
Required checks can run deterministically on each change
when_not_to_use: Checks depend on uncontrolled external state
The workflow would require unapproved secrets or paid services
trigger_conditions: A pull request or commit is proposed for integration
A required verification command or schema changes
workflow_steps: Pin the runner and dependency environment
Run syntax, schema, unit, integration and scoped security checks
Publish exact results tied to the commit SHA
Require current passing statuses and independent review before merge
Quarantine flaky checks instead of silently ignoring them
example_prompt: Review or design CI for this change with deterministic required checks tied to the commit SHA. Block merge on missing or failing evidence and do not claim success from skipped jobs.
ecomdy_example: Illustrative future Ecomdy use: validate future technique data with schema and reference checks before integration without modifying the main registry.
acceptance_criteria: Required checks are deterministic and tied to the exact commit
Missing, failed or stale checks block integration
verification_procedure: Run the CI workflow on a controlled branch and inspect commit-bound results
Test failing and skipped-check fixtures for merge blocking
security_considerations: Protect CI secrets and required statuses
Untrusted PR code must not receive broad credentials or bypass review
fallback_procedure: Run the declared checks manually on the exact commit and record evidence until CI is available.
